text.p: Ecuadorean Finance Minister Pablo Concha promised Friday that the government's economic plan to be presented by the middle of next month will be fiscally austere but boost social programs.
"We are going to present the country with a program of macroeconomic stability, fiscal severity, economic reactivation, and which gives priority to social programs," Concha told local television.
He said that plans to subsidize food and milk for the poor would not cost the government much to implement.
The minister ruled out printing money to finance programs.
"When we talk about the financial support the Central Bank can give the central government, that support does not exist. It is nil," he said.
The first outline of the economic program will be made known when the government presents its 1997 budget bill at the end of the month.

"The state's budget for 1997 is going to contain the first elements of the government's position with respect to its final program. A program which will include a range of drastic measures to recover and extend the base of taxpayers," said Concha.
He added that Ecuadoreans will have to endure a year of austerity while the government aims to balance its books.
Next year will be crucial for the "reordering of the Ecuadorean economy," he said.
Analysts said that one of the government's biggest challenges will be reducing its budget deficit, which is running at four percent of gross domestic product.

The government forecasts Ecuador will finish 1996 with inflation of 25 percent and growth of 2.9 percent. It hopes that next year inflation will subside to 20 percent, and that the economy will grow by four percent.
